subject: Urgent: data transfer clearance & KMS requirement blocking pilot launch
messages:
From: Emily Torres <etorres@fincarehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fincarehealth.com
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed DPA redlines and KMS requirement for pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move the pilot forward. Our legal/procurement team reviewed your standard DPA and attached a redline with several required changes before procurement will sign:

- Key management: we insist on customer-controlled keys (BYOK/HSM) for PHI/PII processing during the pilot.
- Subprocessor visibility: need an up-to-date list and SOC2 attestations for subprocessors that will touch customer data.
- Data transfer: must include SCCs + UK Addendum or an equivalent transfer mechanism documented in the DPA.

We attached our redlines (FinCare_DPA_Redline_20270728.pdf). Procurement needs confirmation and evidence (attestation or architecture note) that Redwood supports KMS/BYOK or an exception approval from your security lead.

Timeline: pilot ingestion window opens 2027-08-09 — procurement requested final DPA execution by 2027-08-05 or we risk delaying the launch. Please escalate if necessary.

Best,
Emily Torres
Head of Product, FinCare Health
etorres@fincarehealth.com
Attachments: FinCare_DPA_Redline_20270728.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <etorres@fincarehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines and KMS requirement for pilot

Emily — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Appreciate the deadline callout.

Quick answers and next steps from our side:
- Subprocessors: attached is our current subprocessors list (redwood_subprocessors_20270727.csv). Happy to surface SOC2 reports for specific vendors — will confirm which ones process pilot data.
- KMS/BYOK: our hosted offering uses provider-managed keys by default. We do support customer key control for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we can provide HSM attestations for the key management controls we rely on, but we do not currently offer BYOK in hosted.

Given the pilot constraints, I will escalate to security/legal for either (A) a documented security attestation + contractual compensating controls for hosted, or (B) an exception allowing limited pilot on hosted under strict retention/segmentation controls. I’m copying Vivek and Rishi to move this along.

Can you confirm whether pilot data will include live PHI? That affects the controls we must propose. If you can share the procurement checklist now, that will help speed validation.

I’ll follow up with an internal timeline later today and aim to have a proposed wording to satisfy procurement by 2027-08-02.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20270727.csv (text/csv)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 13:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Proposed DPA redlines and KMS requirement for pilot

Team — I reviewed FinCare's redline. High-level: we treat customer-controlled KMS as a hard requirement for Private/Dedicated but we sometimes allow hosted pilots under an exception if compensating technical and contractual controls are in place. To evaluate:

1) Does the pilot require storage of identifiable PHI? If yes, exception bar is higher.
2) Can we carve the pilot scope so only pseudonymized tokens are sent to hosted?
3) We need vendor attestations (SOC2 Type II) for any subprocessors that will store or cache request data.

Action items for Kimberly/Rishi:
- Provide an architectural note describing where keys live and whether token-level segmentation can be enforced.
- Provide SOC2/ISO documents for the three main infra vendors that will touch data.

If we cannot get those items by COB Monday (2027-08-02), procurement should be told the pilot risks a delay. I will prepare a short exception template to propose to FinCare that limits retention to 24 hours, prevents model fine-tuning on pilot data, and requires additional logging and audit windows.

Vivek
Chief Security Officer — Redwood Inference
Attachments: security_evidence_request.txt (text/plain)

From: Emily Torres <etorres@fincarehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@fincarehealth.com, Paul Nguyen <pnguyen@legalworks.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Jul 2027 08:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines and KMS requirement for pilot

Kimberly/Vivek — thanks for the quick responses. A few clarifications from procurement/legal:

- Pilot WILL process live PHI (masked fields, but still considered PHI under our program).
- Procurement cannot accept 'attestations' alone — they need either (a) BYOK/BYOK-HSM (customer-managed keys), or (b) documented and signed exception with explicit retention and audit clauses + a list of subprocessors with SOC2 artifacts.
- DocuSign: procurement asked that any accepted redlines be captured in a single signed document (they prefer a single executed DPA + any addenda via DocuSign).

Attached is our procurement checklist for your security team to confirm items. If we don't have explicit CISO sign-off by 2027-08-02, we will have to postpone the ingestion window. Can your security team commit to either (A) preparing the exception + controls today, or (B) scheduling a call to finalize BYOK feasibility and timeline?

Appreciate the urgency — this pilot matters for our Q4 roadmap.

Emily
Attachments: FinCare_ProcurementChecklist.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Torres <etorres@fincarehealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Aug 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed DPA redlines and KMS requirement for pilot — proposed path forward

Emily — thank you and sorry for the pressure. Quick status and proposed path that should keep your launch date intact if accepted: 

1) Exception + controls: Vivek will provide a one-page exception addendum that limits retention to 24 hours, disables model tuning, requires encrypted request logging, and mandates notification to FinCare within 24 hours of any subprocessor change. This is similar to our standard temporary-pilot addendum. We will commit to including SOC2 artifacts for subprocessors that touch pilot data.

2) DocuSign packaging: legal will prepare a single DPA addendum package (base DPA + exception addendum + transfer clause language) and route via DocuSign. I have asked Legal to pre-populate fields so procurement can sign without additional redlines. Link will be provided when ready: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/EX-987654321

3) Contingency (BYOK): If FinCare requires BYOK for the pilot, we will need Dedicated or Private deployment. We can scope a limited Dedicated pool for the pilot, but that adds procurement lead time (est. 3-4 weeks).

Request from procurement/legal side: please confirm whether you can accept the exception addendum + SOC2 artifacts as sufficient for execution by 2027-08-05. If yes, I will ask Rishi/Marissa to finalize the DocuSign bundle and get Vivek's one-page addendum signed. If no, we should schedule an urgent call today to discuss Dedicated onboarding.

I'll follow up with the DocuSign package link and the exception text later today.

Thanks — appreciate your flexibility.
Kimberly Park
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Attachments: docusign-envelope-link.txt (text/plain)
